findings.reason: parse_link_destination.mjs:52 now breaks at the backslash, so the destination is `foo` and result.pos points at the backslash. Before, `pos++; continue` moved to the space and then broke at line 46, giving `foo\`. In link.mjs:55-76 the whitespace skip stops at the backslash and the `)` check fails, so the link falls back to a reference and fails; the bundled spec treats a backslash before a non-punctuation character as literal. Severity set to medium, between C1's high and X1's medium: the trigger is traced, but the input is a narrow edge case and the locked fixture `[link](a\ b)` (commonmark_extras.txt:345) gives the same output before and after.
findings.claim: When a link destination has a backslash followed by a space, the parser now stops before the backslash instead of keeping the backslash and stopping at the space. Inline links, images and reference definitions such as `[a](foo\ )` therefore no longer parse.
findings.evidence: The diff replaces `if (str.charCodeAt(pos + 1) === 0x20) { pos++; continue }` with `{ break }`, so `result.pos` now points at the `\` instead of the space. In lib/rules_inline/link.mjs:54-76, the whitespace skip starts at `\`, skips nothing, `start === pos` so no title is taken, and `state.src.charCodeAt(pos) !== 0x29` sets `parseReference = true`, so the inline link fails. In lib/rules_block/reference.mjs:118-173, `pos = destEndPos` lands on `\` and fails the `str.charCodeAt(pos) !== 0x0A` end-of-line check, so the reference definition is rejected. Before the change, the destination was `foo\` and the parser stopped at the space. CommonMark allows a backslash before a non-punctuation character in a destination as a literal, so `foo\` is a valid destination. The locked fixture `[link](a\ b)` (commonmark_extras.txt:345) is not a link under either version, so it does not tell the old and new behaviour apart.
